knowledge_point.title: Determining Whether a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors

question.:question/problem:
The vectors $\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are given below. Determine whether $\mathbf{b}\in \operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2}\}$. In the affirmative case, find $x_{1}\cdot x_{2}$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{b}=x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}$.
$\mathbf{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}$
$\mathbf{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}$
$\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}$
question.:question/worked-solution:
By the definition of span, $\mathbf{b}\in \operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2}\}$ exactly when coefficients exist such that

$$
x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}=\mathbf{b}.
$$

Equating components gives

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1}-2x_{2} &= -2 \\ -x_{1}+2x_{2} &= 3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Set up the augmented matrix and use elementary row operations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & -2 \\ -1 & 2 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

$$
R_{2}\leftarrow R_{2}-\left(-1\right)R_{1}
$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

Row $2$ gives $0=1$, a contradiction. No coefficients satisfy every component, so $\mathbf{b}\notin \operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2}\}$.

knowledge_point.title: Determining Whether a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors

question.:question/problem:
The vectors $\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are given below. Determine whether $\mathbf{b}\in \operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2}\}$. In the affirmative case, find $x_{1}\cdot x_{2}$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{b}=x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}$.
$\mathbf{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}$
$\mathbf{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}$
$\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix}-4 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}$
question.:question/worked-solution:
By the definition of span, $\mathbf{b}\in \operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2}\}$ exactly when coefficients exist such that

$$
x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}=\mathbf{b}.
$$

Equating components gives

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2x_{1}+x_{2} &= -4 \\ x_{2} &= 2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Set up the augmented matrix and use elementary row operations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-2 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Back-substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x_{2} &= \frac{2}{1} = 2 \\ x_{1} &= \frac{-4-\left(1\right)\left(2\right)}{-2} = 3\end{aligned}
$$

All component equations hold. Thus $\mathbf{b}\in \operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2}\}$ and the coefficients are unique. Finally,

$$
x_{1}\cdot x_{2}=\left(3\right)\cdot \left(2\right)=6.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Determining Whether a Vector Lies in the Span of Given Vectors

question.:question/problem:
The vectors $\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are given below. Determine whether $\mathbf{b}\in \operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2}\}$. In the affirmative case, find $x_{1}\cdot x_{2}$ from the decomposition $\mathbf{b}=x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}$.
$\mathbf{a}_{1}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}$
$\mathbf{a}_{2}=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}$
$\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix}-2 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}$
question.:question/worked-solution:
By the definition of span, $\mathbf{b}\in \operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2}\}$ exactly when coefficients exist such that

$$
x_{1}\mathbf{a}_{1}+x_{2}\mathbf{a}_{2}=\mathbf{b}.
$$

Equating components gives

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-x_{1}+x_{2} &= -2 \\ -x_{1}+x_{2} &= -3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Set up the augmented matrix and use elementary row operations:

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-1 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

$$
R_{2}\leftarrow R_{2}-\left(1\right)R_{1}
$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}-1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

Row $2$ gives $0=-1$, a contradiction. No coefficients satisfy every component, so $\mathbf{b}\notin \operatorname{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_{1},\mathbf{a}_{2}\}$.
